Tenzin joined us on Monday, and Nirmala, twenty-four, has been teaching Tenzin pattern grading. Today the export order was due by four, and Tenzin's extra-large sleeve came out too narrow. Wed, 11 pm
Jatin's first week at the station. Tonight he had to cut a ten-minute interview into a three-minute clip for the morning show, and I could have done it in fifteen minutes. My fingers actually hovered over his keyboard.
Instead I asked what he'd tried. He'd cut from the start and run out of time before the good part. One hint: find the best thirty seconds first, then build around it. Then I made myself go and refill the water jug.
He took nearly an hour. We missed the eleven o'clock handover, and the producer gave me a look.
But the clip was good. Better than mine would have been, honestly, because he kept the bit where the fisherman laughs.
Next week he'll do it in twenty minutes, and I'll have a colleague, not a trainee. Worth one look from the producer.
Amandeep

At the government school in a village near Latur, Rajni, twenty-five, had taught the combined Class 3 and 4 for two years. Rafiq had joined in June, fresh from training, and was drowning.
"The Class 3s keep interrupting while I teach Class 4," he said at lunch. "I don't know what to do."
Rajni's first urge was to walk in and take over his class. It would have been faster.
Instead she asked, "What have you tried?"
"Shouting. Giving them colouring. Nothing works."
"One idea. Give Class 3 a task they can do in pairs for fifteen minutes, then switch."
Rafiq tried it the next day. It half worked. He came back with a question about pairing. She answered only that.
By August his classroom was quieter than hers. She laughed about it, and meant it.

qa.a: In June.

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling when she held back the urge to take over?
qa.a: She felt tempted and a little impatient, but chose patience so Rafiq could learn himself.

qa.q: Why was Rajni's slower approach wise?
qa.a: Asking what he'd tried and giving one idea let Rafiq build his own skill, creating a capable colleague instead of dependence.

qa.q: How might Rafiq feel by August?
qa.a: He probably felt more confident and proud, running a calmer classroom he had learned to manage himself.

grounding: It shows a junior teacher coaching a new colleague with one hint, resisting taking over, and building a capable teacher.

At the bakery in Montreal, it was 5 am and the croissant dough was misbehaving. Sofia, the new baker, stood over it with butter oozing out the sides.
Leila, twenty-six, had been there three years. She could fix it in two minutes. The café opened at seven.
She folded her arms instead. "What have you tried?"
"I chilled it. I rolled it again. The butter keeps breaking through."
"One thing: how cold is your butter compared to the dough?"
Sofia paused. "Colder. Much colder."
"Hmm."
Sofia's eyes widened. She took the butter out to soften for ten minutes, then tried again. The layers held.
The first tray came out a bit uneven. Leila didn't say anything about that. She just said, "Tomorrow, you'll do it faster."
They opened at 7:10. Leila decided it was worth it.

Dear Kavitha,
I wanted to tell you something I learned this week, since you're about to start training new staff too.
Our new hire, Priyam, was struggling with a client report. My instinct was to redo it myself; it would have taken me twenty minutes and saved the deadline.
Instead I asked, "What have you tried?" Priyam walked me through it. I offered one hint: "Start with the summary, then the numbers." Then I made myself walk away.
It took Priyam two hours. The report wasn't perfect. But the next one came to me almost done, with no questions.
Slower now, faster later. That's what I'm learning.
Siddharth

qa.a: Priyam may have felt stretched but trusted, and more capable by the next report.

"You asked what surprised me most about managing people. I'm Hansa, I've been a nurse supervisor for a year now, and honestly, it's how hard it is not to help.
There's a new nurse, Shreya. Her first week, she had trouble setting up a drip line. I could have done it in thirty seconds.

That's when I understood. My job isn't to do it fastest. It's to make her able to do it without me."
